text.en: Akbar wanted to know how many crows were in the city. Birbal said, “Exactly 963.” “What if there are fewer?” “Some have gone on holiday.” “What if more?” “Visitors have come.” Akbar was pleased.

Welcome to House of Hundreds Two. Akbar and Birbal were walking in a garden watching crows. Birbal said there were 963 crows in the city, and cleverly explained any difference.
Three-digit numbers are made of hundreds, tens and ones. Draw tiles to show 832, 947, 726, 504, 620 and 700.
Locate numbers on a number line. 530 and 540 are close, 628 lies between 620 and 660, and 696 is just before 700.
The Number Detective game has special numbers. 100, 200, 300 are hundreds. 123, 345 and 789 have digits going up. 876 and 321 go down.
Numbers like 11, 22, 33 have twin digits and 111, 222, 333 have triplet digits.
Numbers like 353 and 868 look the same from left to right and from right to left. These are called palindromes (additional, not in the textbook).
Make numbers with paper slips marked 100, 10 and 1. With 6 slips you can make 420 with four 100s and two 10s? Check how many hundreds and tens you need.
To make 231 you need two slips of 100, three of 10 and one of 1.
